key_insight: LES grid resolution changes predicted hurricane wind and turbulence structures, producing distinct aeroelastic responses in an idling wind turbine.
engineering_relevance: High-resolution hurricane inflow information can improve extreme-load prediction and support wind turbine design in cyclone-prone regions.
method: Simulate Hurricane Laura (2020) using large-eddy simulation at grid spacings of 55.55, 25, and 10 m.
Compare mean winds and turbulence structures as the storm passes a virtual turbine location.
Use LES fields directly as inflow for aeroelastic simulations of an idling turbine.
evidence_signal: The three-resolution comparison revealed significant differences in mean winds and turbulent structures, with distinct impacts on simulated turbine response.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantified load differences or grid-convergence assessment, so the accuracy gains from finer resolution remain unquantified.
paper_title: Hurricane Laura-induced loads on wind turbines -- Part I: High-fidelity modeling and sensitivity to turbulent inflow conditions
